sections.title: Preflight Inspection
sections.notes: Items marked with an asterisk (*) are to be checked prior to the first flight of the day and may be omitted for subsequent flights that day.

items.text: * Lap belt and shoulder harness: Webbing
* Lap belt and shoulder harness: Release buckle
* Canopy actuating mechanism (handles, rollers and tracks)
Obtain fuel sampler from map compartment
Lap belt and shoulder harness: Webbing
Lap belt and shoulder harness: Release buckle
* Canopy actuating mechanism (handles, rollers and tracks)
Shoulder harness, seat belt, seat cushion and any loose equipment
Top and bottom of wing surfaces for cracks, tears, wrinkles, bulges, deep scratches and popped rivets.
Flaps and tracks for visible damage
Aileron: a. Bellcrank, trim tab connections secure.
Aileron: b. Trim tab for servo action, faired with aileron at zero deflection, hinge bolt facing fuselage, nut cotter-keyed, bolt head clear of flap when aileron moved.
Static discharge wicks for fraying, deterioration, and proper attachment (min length 6" overall, 1" exposed).
Dents, scratches and condition of navigation light.
Stall warning vane for freedom of movement.
Landing light for security of lens and bulb.
Pitot tube: Cover removed, tube aligned, secure and clear.
Visually check fuel quantity, fuel cap chain secure at both ends, "O" ring for cuts & cracks. Replace cap securely.
Cockpit air intake screen for obstructions.
Spar cap for corrosion, adjacent wing skin for bulges.
Undersurface for evidence of fuel leakage.
Condition of main gear doors, wheel well free of obstructions.
Uplock bracket spring attached to uplock bracket & wing rib.
Small spring inside canvas dust cover attached to uplock cable and uplock bracket.
Uplock mechanism for distortion and security.
Roller on landing gear brace for freedom of movement.
Shock strut for scoring and pitting, piston for evidence of leakage and approximately 3 inches of strut extension.
Hydraulic fittings for condition and leaks.
Tire for condition and proper inflation.
Fuel tank vent tube slanted forward approximately 15 degrees with bias cut facing forward.
Skin for damage and excessive oil or hydraulic fluid.
Open access panel 4, take fuel sample from fuel sump, ensure drain valve closed and secure access panel.
Open access panel 7, take fuel sample from fuel strainer, ensure drain valve closed and secure access panel.
NOTE: FUEL SHUTOFF VALVE HANDLE MUST BE ON TO DRAIN FUEL STRAINER.
Apron under engine for excessive oil or fuel leakage.
Check oil level. MIN: 10 QTS COLD, 11 QTS HOT. Filler cap retaining chain securely attached at both ends.
Check for fuel / oil leaks, frayed / broken wires, chafed lines, cracked exhaust stacks and broken or loose heater ducts
Check fuel filter drain valve safety wired in closed position.
Check red plunger flush with top of fuel filter assembly.
Prop governor cable not chafing on fuel filter bracket.
Check alternate air door closed and linkage secure.
Check left augmentor tube for obstructions.
Centering mechanism, bracket, retract arm for looseness.
Check nose gear centering roller is free to rotate.
Uplock mechanism for distortion and security.
Shimmy damper for evidence of leakage and damage.
Shock strut for scoring and pitting, piston for leakage and approximately 5 inches of strut extension.
Mud scraper for security and obvious damage.
Grounding wire for security and touching the deck.
Nose tire for condition and proper inflation.
Propeller for cracks, nicks, pits, and evidence of oil leakage. Inspect security of spinner retention nut.
Air intake, filter, hot air overboard inlets clean, unobstructed. Ensure lock fasteners firmly secured.
Check for fuel / oil leaks, frayed / broken wires, chafed lines, cracked exhaust stacks and broken or loose heater ducts.
Generator capacitor securely clamped, clear of cowling arm.
Check right augmentor tube for obstructions.
Security of external canopy release handle.
Check connector and holding bar security.
Check for evidence of electrolyte leakage, warps and bulges.
Check drain hoses connected to case.
Close battery compartment door and secure latches.
Check for evidence of electrolyte overflow and contamination.
Close battery drain jar compartment door and secure latch.
Perform same checks as for left main landing gear.
Perform same checks as on left wing except for pitot tube and stall warning vane. Check stall strip for security.
Check condition of antennas and strobe light on belly.
Check for wrinkled skin and popped rivets.
Check static vent free of obstructions.
Check VOR antenna and rotating beacon for security.
All tail surfaces for cracks, corrosion, dents and tears; control surfaces for freedom of movement, looseness and excessive play between elevators.
All visible control linkages and hinge fittings for cracks and security; rudder trim tab for anti-servo action.
VHF antenna and retaining nut for corrosion and security.
Navigation light and tail cone for security and cracks.
Static discharge wicks for fraying, deterioration and proper attachment. (min length 6", 1" exposed wick).
Check for wrinkled skin and popped rivets.
Check static vent is free of obstructions.
Ensure tow bar, spare oil, log book and personal items are properly stowed in the baggage compartment.
Ensure weight and balance are within limits.
Close and lock baggage compartment door.
Ensure wheel chocks and tiedowns are removed and location of nearest fire bottle is noted. Ensure all frost, snow or ice is removed from all aircraft surfaces before flight.

items.response: ON, Checked by outside observer, then OFF

items.text: Navigation and external gear down lights
COLD ENGINE: 4 SECONDS MAX TO AVOID FLOODING
HOT ENGINE: MIXTURE FULL RICH AS ENGINE FIRES
(No rise in 10 seconds or 30 psi in 30 seconds, secure engine.)
MIXTURE LEVER TO RPM ON QUADRANT
If engine fails to start after 15 seconds:
Crank 5 seconds, then repeat steps 3 thru 12. If engine fails to start after 10 seconds, perform steps 22 through 28.
Allow starter to cool for 5 minutes, repeat steps 3 thru 12.
If still no start, secure engine and request assistance.
DO NOT EXCEED 1400 RPM UNTIL OIL TEMP IS AT LEAST 40 DEGREES C

sections.title: Ground Burnout
sections.condition: If, after extended taxi or idle time, the ignition system checks out of limits, proceed as follows:

items.response: LEAN TO 50 RPM DROP BELOW BEST POWER

items.text: If system does not check out
Accelerate in ground effect to at least 70 KIAS
High sink rates can develop at approach speeds below 65 KIAS flaps down with power at idle, leading to a potential hard landing. Power must be increased during the flare to prevent dropping in.
On touchdown, apply maximum braking and full aft stick.
Establish positive rate of climb - Vx
